mission_07: The indicator variable approach treats missingness as potentially informative rather than just a nuisance. When data is Missing Not at Random (MNAR), the fact that a value is missing may itself carry predictive information. For example, people with high incomes may be less likely to report their salary, or patients with severe symptoms may skip certain survey questions. The approach creates binary indicator columns (1 if missing, 0 if observed) for each variable with missing values, then imputes the actual values. Both the imputed values and the indicators are used as features, allowing the model to learn from both the estimated values and the pattern of missingness. sklearn SimpleImputer supports this natively with the add_indicator parameter, making implementation straightforward.
